protocol.description: This protocol lets a client ask the compositor to keep a toplevel's content at a fixed aspect ratio, the way the ICCCM aspect hints in WM_NORMAL_HINTS do for X11 clients. The compositor applies the ratio to every size it chooses for the window, including the sizes it sends while the user resizes the window interactively, so the content keeps its shape during the resize rather than after it.

interface.name: luma_window_shape_manager_v1
interface.description: A global that gives toplevels a luma_window_shape_v1 object.

entry.name: already_constructed
entry.summary: the surface already has a luma_window_shape_v1 object

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys the manager. Objects created through it are not affected.

request.name: get_window_shape

description.summary: get the shape object of a surface

request.description:
Creates the shape object of the given surface. A surface has at most one; asking for a second one while the first exists is the already_constructed protocol error.
The object takes a wl_surface rather than an xdg_toplevel so that toolkits which keep their xdg_toplevel private can use it. Its state has an effect only while the surface has the xdg_toplevel role, and it stays with the surface if the role object is destroyed and created again.

interface.name: luma_window_shape_v1
interface.description: The shape constraints of the xdg_toplevel of one wl_surface. The set_aspect_ratio and unset_aspect_ratio requests are double buffered: they take effect on the next wl_surface.commit, like xdg_toplevel.set_min_size. Once the surface is destroyed, requests are ignored; the object should then be destroyed.

entry.name: invalid_aspect_ratio
entry.summary: width or height is zero, or a value is out of range

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys the object. The window loses its aspect ratio at once.

request.name: set_aspect_ratio

description.summary: keep the content at a fixed aspect ratio

request.description:
Asks the compositor to keep the window geometry, less base_width and base_height, at width:height. The base is the part of the window geometry that does not scale with the content, such as a header bar; it is in surface-local coordinates. Only the ratio of width and height matters: 4:3 and 640:480 are the same request.
The compositor applies the ratio when the window floats, both to the sizes it suggests in configure events, including those it sends with the resizing state, and to sizes the client picks itself. For a maximized window the compositor may choose the largest size with the ratio that fits the area the window would otherwise fill. It does not apply the ratio to fullscreen windows, and it may ignore it for tiled windows, whose size is given by the tile: a client should still be ready to letterbox its content in any size it is configured to.
width and height must be greater than zero and at most 65535, and the base at most 65535 in each direction, or the invalid_aspect_ratio error is raised.

arg.name: base_width
arg.summary: width of the window geometry outside the content

arg.name: base_height
arg.summary: height of the window geometry outside the content

request.name: unset_aspect_ratio

description.summary: let the window take any shape again

request.description: Removes the aspect ratio set with set_aspect_ratio.
